text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read and understand, so developers can find and fix problems faster. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller parts, or remove repeated code. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the behaviour must stay exactly the same. Regular refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly and carelessly. In short, clean code saves time and money in the long run.
